properties.decision:
DECIDED — Anthony, 2026-08-09, answering dec:idea-governance-management-split: "my decision is not to split governance/management out from reflow2, but integrate it properly into reflow2."

Governance and management stay inside reflow2. No sister package, no second binary, no separate vocabulary. The work that follows is INTEGRATION work.

ANTHONY'S DIAGNOSIS, and it is the part that changes what happens next: "it is kind of the late addition, so that is probably why it isn't very well connected/integrated into reflow2 — so we're playing a little bit of catch up."

This reclassifies the evidence rather than dismissing it. Every observation that looked like a case for splitting is re-read as arrears owed by a late arrival:
- DesignRule being "the least-connected type in the schema, which is odd for the one whose whole job is to bind other things" (storyflow trial case, 2026-08-09) is not a sign the type belongs elsewhere. It is a sign the type was added after the edges were drawn.
- dec:bl-155's finding that ~17 of the 40 never-called tools are the management/governance/coordination family is not evidence of an unwanted surface. BL-155's own conclusion already said these tools are UNREACHABLE FROM ANY SKILL rather than unwanted, and a late addition is exactly what fails to get wired into the skills that would name it.
- reflow2's eight functional systems (dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition) containing no management or governance system is, on this reading, the same debt stated structurally: the decomposition was drawn before the concern arrived and was never revised to hold it.

WHY THIS IS A DECISION AND NOT A PREFERENCE: it settles what to do with every future governance finding. The question stops being "does this belong here?" and becomes "what is it not yet connected to?" — which is answerable from the graph, unlike the first.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DECIDE: it does not say governance vocabulary must be mandatory for every project, and it does not rule out the optional-profile shape (option C of the brainstorm) as an INTERNAL organising idea. It rules out the PACKAGE split only. It also does not say the integration is small — the storyflow fleet sized the missing primitives as "a small declarative field plus a report — not a subsystem", and that estimate is theirs, not confirmed here.

CONSISTENT WITH the accepted requirements the split would have cost: req:thin-install and req:no-setup-per-project both survive untouched, which they would not have under a second package. And with proj:reflow2's objective, "keep a design coherent from concept through operations", which names the whole lifecycle as scope rather than design alone.

SUPERSEDES dec:idea-governance-management-split, which stays on the record with all four options so the roads not taken remain visible.
properties.name: Governance and management stay in reflow2 and get properly integrated — the weak connection is catch-up debt from a late addition, not a boundary asking to be drawn
properties.rationale: Anthony's word, given directly on 2026-08-09 after the brainstorm was put to him. The reasoning worth preserving is his causal one: governance arrived late, so its poor integration is chronology rather than architecture — which means the fix is wiring, not relocation. Recorded because a later session finding governance badly connected would otherwise be entitled to re-open the split question, and this says it was asked and answered.
